name: Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck (Tiroler Museumsbahnen)
kurzbeschreibung: The Localbahn Museum in the old Stubaital train station in Innsbruck: historic trams, locomotives, and Tyrolean railway history since 1891.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historically significant Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck – operated by the Tiroler Museumsbahnen (TMB) association – is located at the foot of Bergisel in the Wilten district of Innsbruck at Pater-Reinisch-Weg 4, at an altitude of around 590 meters. Housed in the listed depot and workshop rooms of the former Stubaital train station from 1904, this specialized museum is one of the most important collections of railway history in Central Europe. It documents the pioneering development of the Tyrolean Alpine valleys through electric local railways, cog railways, and trams from the late 19th century onwards.

Route & Requirements

The origins of the collection date back to 1983, when railway enthusiasts founded the association to save historic Tyrolean rail vehicles. The exhibition hall houses over 25 historic original rail vehicles, lovingly and operationally restored by volunteer members. Highlights include railcars of the legendary Stubaitalbahn – the world's first full-gauge railway operated with high-voltage alternating current (opened in 1904) – historic wagons of the Innsbruck tram, the Innsbrucker Mittelgebirgsbahn (Line 6), as well as vehicles from the Ritten Railway and the Bolzano tram. Information boards, historical photographs, historical ticket printers, uniforms, signal boards, and detailed model railway layouts illustrate the enormous engineering achievement of Alpine railway construction during the Austro-Hungarian monarchy. On selected weekends in summer, the museum organizes nostalgic rides with historic tram trains through the Innsbruck city area.

Visit & Arrival

The Localbahnmuseum Innsbruck is open to visitors on Saturdays from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM during the summer months from early May to late October (guided tours for groups of 10 or more people are possible year-round on weekdays by prior arrangement). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and teenagers (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €14.00. Admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck main station, take tram line 1 to the Bergisel stop or the Stubaitalbahn (STB) directly to the Stubaitalbahnhof stop (only a one-minute walk to the museum). By car: Via the Brennerautobahn A13 (Innsbruck Süd exit), parking available at the Bergisel ski jump or along Pater-Reinisch-Weg.

Tips

The historic vehicle hall and workshop rooms are step-free and wheelchair accessible; some historic wagons have narrow entry steps. For railway fans and children, climbing onto the historic wooden benches in the old trams is an unforgettable experience. Combine your visit with a scenic ride on the Stubaitalbahn through the Telfer meadows to Fulpmes.
